dossiers.label: The eye that sees itself
dossiers.about: What does the Delphic 'know thyself' mean? If it said to an eye 'see thyself', the eye would look into another eye, at the pupil where its image appears as in a mirror. So the soul, to know itself, must look at soul, and at the part where wisdom comes to be, the most godlike part.

passage.end_quote: οὕτω καὶ ἑαυτὸν ἂν γνοίη μάλιστα

parts.label: If it said to the eye 'see thyself'
parts.quote: εἰ ἡμῶν τῷ ὄμματι ὥσπερ ἀνθρώπῳ συμβουλεῦον εἶπεν ἰδὲ σαυτόν

parts.label: The face appears in the pupil as in a mirror
parts.quote: ὥσπερ ἐν κατόπτρῳ, ὃ δὴ καὶ κόρην καλοῦμεν

parts.label: So the soul must look into soul
parts.quote: καὶ ψυχὴ εἰ μέλλει γνώσεσθαι αὑτήν, εἰς ψυχὴν αὐτῇ βλεπτέον

parts.label: The godlike part; knowing god, it knows itself
parts.quote: τῷ θεῷ ἄρα τοῦτʼ ἔοικεν αὐτῆς

related.why: Socrates in the Phaedrus has no time for myths: he cannot yet know himself.
In the Phaedrus too the lover sees himself in the beloved as in a mirror.

web.title: Alcibiades I
web.quote: the famous Delphic phrase: gnōthi seautón meaning know thyself
